To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the frequency of chromosome alterations in B61 cells is 7-fold higher compared with A31 parental cells; 2) the frequency of RLC in B61 cells (1.95/cells) is 7-fold greater than in A31 cells (0.25/cell); 3) the frequency of LTS' and LTS" in B61 cells was 3-fold higher than in A31; 4) ITS were detected at both non telomeric sites and

1) The frequencies of RBCs with ITS located at the centromeres are significantly higher in ras-transfacted than in normal Balb/3 T3 cells; 2) The frequency of LTS' and LTS" are significantly higher in the ras-transfected than in the normal Balb/ 3T3 cells; 3) The frequencies of chromosome alterations with telomeric signals are higher in ras-transfact cells than in normal Bal/3T3;
the frequency of telomere alterations is increased in ras-transfeted cells, and the centromeric localization of telomeric sequences is associated with a more severe phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of telomeres in the process of carcinogenesis.
the study of telomeric sequences in mouse fibroblasts and the possible involvement of telomeric DNA in chromosome rearrangements.

the study of telomeric DNA alterations in cells with different levels of chromosome instability, which may be of interest to the understanding of telomere function and the role of telomeric regions in the maintenance of chromosome stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ha-ras-1 oncogene induces chromosome rearrangements involving the telomere DNA sequences, but the mechanism of action of ras in this process is still unknown.
the presence of an activated oncogene in the genome of Balb/3 T3 cells is a predisposition to a higher level of chromosome instability, which could be related to the high level of cell proliferation.
ras-transfected mouse fibroblast cells show an increase in the frequency of telomeric chromosome alterations, which may be associated with an accelerated cell cycle progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ha-ras oncoprotein is able to induce telomeric instability and chromosome rearrangements, which are probably related to the immortalization process.
telomeric DNA instability may be involved in the development and progression of tumours.

ras oncogene transfection in Balb/ 3T3 mouse cells leads to the formation of RLC with ITS in the centromere, and that these cells are unstable with high frequencies of chromosome rearrangements involving ITS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ha-ras gene can be involved in the generation of chromosome aberrations in mammalian cells, and the frequency of these events is dependent on the expression of the oncogene.
telomeric DNA can be involved in chromosomal rearrangements and can be detected in the centromere of chromosomes with RLC configurations.
the presence of the oncogene ras is associated with the appearance of a new type of RLCs in which the centromeres are involved.
